{{Short description|Measure of spatial correlation}}

'''Tjøstheim's coefficient'''<ref>
{{cite journal
| doi = 10.1093/biomet/65.1.109
| author = D. Tjøstheim 
| year = 1978
| title = A measure of association for spatial variables
| journal = Biometrika
| volume = 65
| issue = 1
| pages = 109–114 
| jstor = 2335284 
}}
</ref> is a measure of spatial [[correlation|association]] that attempts to quantify the degree to which two spatial data sets are related. Developed by Norwegian statistician [[Dag Tjøstheim]]. It is similar to rank correlation coefficients like [[Spearman's rank correlation coefficient]] and the [[Kendall rank correlation coefficient]] but also explicitly considers the spatial relationship between variables.

Consider two variables, <math>F(x,y)</math> and <math>G(x,y)</math>, observed at the same set of <math>N</math> spatial locations with co-ordinates <math>x_i</math> and <math>y_i</math>. The Rank of <math>F</math> at <math>(x_i,y_i)</math> is

:<math>R_F(x_i,y_i) = \sum_i^N \theta(F(x_i,y_i) - F(x_j,y_j) )</math>

with a similar definition for <math>G</math>. Here <math>\theta</math> is a [[Heaviside step function|step function]] and this formula counts how many values <math>F(x_j,y_j)</math> are less than or equal to the value at the target point <math>F(x_i,y_i)</math>.

Now define
:<math>X_F(i) = \sum_j^N x_j \delta(i, R_F(x_j,y_j))</math>

where <math>\delta</math> is the [[Kronecker delta]]. This is the <math>x</math> coordinate of the <math>i^{\text{th}}</math> ranked <math>F</math> value. The quantities <math>Y_F(i), X_G(i)</math> and <math>Y_G(i)</math> can be defined similarly.

Tjøstheim's coefficient is defined by<ref>
{{cite book
|last1=Vallejos 
|first1= Ronny
|last2=Osorio 
|first2= Feilpe
|last3=Bevilacqua 
|first3= Moreno
|date=2020 
|title=Spatial relationships between two georeferenced variables: With applications in R
|publisher=Springer Cham
|isbn=978-3-030-56681-4
|doi = 10.1007/978-3-030-56681-4
}}</ref>

:<math> A = \frac{\sum_i^N (X_F(i) - \bar{X}_F)(X_G(i) - \bar{X}_G) + (Y_F(i) - \bar{Y}_F)(Y_G(i) - \bar{Y}_G) }{\left(\sum_i^N\left[(X_F(i) - \bar{X}_F)^2 + (Y_F(i) - \bar{Y}_F)^2\right] \sum_i^N\left[(X_G(i) - \bar{X}_G)^2 + (Y_G(i) - \bar{Y}_G)^2\right] \right)^{1/2}}</math>

Under the assumptions that <math>F</math> and <math>G</math> are [[independent and identically distributed random variables]] and are [[Independence (probability theory)|independent]] of each other it can be shown that <math>E[A] = 0</math> and

:<math>var(A) = \frac{\left(\sum_i^N x_i^2\right)^2 + 2 \left(\sum_i^N x_i y_i\right)^2 + \left(\sum_i^N y_i^2\right)^2 }{(N-1)\left(\sum_i^N x_i^2 + \sum_i^N y_i^2\right)^2 }</math>

The maximum variance of <math>1/(N-1)</math> occurs when all points are on a straight line and the minimum variance of <math>1/(2(N-1))</math> occurs for a symmetric cross pattern where <math>x_i y_i = 0</math> and <math>\sum_i^N x_i^2 = \sum_i^N y_i^2</math>.<ref name="Glick">
{{cite journal
| doi = 10.1111/j.1538-4632.1982.tb00066.x
| author = B.J. Glick 
| year = 1982
| title = A Spatial Rank-Order Correlation Measure
| journal = Geographical Analysis
| volume = 14
| issue = 2
| pages = 177–181 
}}
</ref>

Tjøstheim's coefficient is implemented as ''cor.spatial'' in the [[R (programming language)|R]] package SpatialPack.<ref>http://spatialpack.mat.utfsm.cl</ref> Numerical simulations suggest that <math>A</math> is an effective measure of correlation between variables but is sensitive to the degree of [[autocorrelation]] in <math>F</math> and <math>G</math>.<ref name="Glick"/>
